answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to lock a refundable stake in escrow before it can trade. Creating a thousand fake agents then means locking a thousand stakes, so the attacker cost scales linearly with the size of the fraud. Like a harbor that only admits ships flying a registered flag, the market admits only staked identities; a bridge of verified attestations links each stake to real past work, and misbehavior burns the stake like ferrous scrap, worthless after the fire. Honest agents get their stake back; attackers pay per fake.
